New Filing Provides First Clear Look at the Refreshed Honda Accord, Revealing New Face and Logo
6 photos
Photo: GAC-Honda / MIIT filing
Honda prepares a new refresh for the Accord sedan, and, thanks to a regulatory filing in China, we now know how it will look. The Accord will get split headlights and a new grille, as well as Honda's redesigned logo. On the powertrain front, the Chinese Accord will gain the trusted hybrid powertrain based on the 2.0-liter gasoline engine that is also sold in the US.
The eleventh-generation Honda Accord is getting a little long in the tooth, which means that it's time for a mid-cycle refresh. The Japanese sedan is not selling as well as it used to, and that's most obvious in China, where this generation hasn't convinced many customers. Sales have dropped sharply immediately after launch, and Honda thinks the design was to blame.
This might explain why the refreshed model tries to address this with a radical makeover, as revealed in a new regulatory filing with China's MIIT. Instead of the classic looks of today, the refreshed Accord will have split headlights, with a narrow strip incorporating turn signals and the daytime running lights. These may be joined by a light strip, but we haven't seen them lit yet, so it's just speculation. The redesigned Accord also adopts Honda's new frameless logo.
There are no notable changes in other areas of the bodywork. The revised model does feature new side skirts and a slightly redesigned rear bumper, but that's about it. The connected taillights continue their career, only this time they integrate the Accord lettering. The Honda logo has been repositioned higher, on the trunk lid.
Photo: GAC-Honda / MIIT filing The MIIT filing doesn't provide pictures of the interior, but it does show close-ups of the Accord's available options. These include a lip spoiler, a pop-up sunroof, as well as several ADAS sensor configurations. According to the document, the updated sedan measures 4,986 mm (196.3 in), thus being 4 mm (0.15 in) shorter than its predecessor. The wheelbase remains unchanged, at 2,830 mm (111.4 in).
The Chinese market also gets a hybrid powertrain sourced from the global-spec Accord, which is also sold in the US. Besides the turbocharged 1.5-liter engine and the 2.0-liter plug-in of the e:PHEV variant, the refreshed model adds a self-charging hybrid based on the same 2.0-liter engine.
The combustion engine develops 146 horsepower and is helped by electric motors and a Li-ion battery supplied by Dalian Taixing Energy. No combined output is stated, but the US-spec Accord e:HEV develops 204 horsepower in a similar configuration. The top speed of the Chinese-market sedan is rated at 198 kph (123 mph).
There's little chance that the refreshed Accord will be offered in the US with similar design changes. Most likely, the US model will continue in its current form until the 12th generation, expected to launch around 2028. This will be underpinned by a new modular architecture, with style inspired by the Honda Hybrid Sedan Prototype .
